props.gloss_en: the mishnah: that which comes out of the impure [animal] is impure, and that which comes out of the pure is pure
the urine of a donkey -- what [is its law]? Is it drawn from its body and so forbidden, or perhaps water goes in and water comes out, and its turbidity is the heat of the flesh?
the urine of horses and camels raised no question: it is not turbid and not like milk -- water goes in, water comes out
Rav Sheshet: you learned it -- the mishnah says not 'from an impure one' but 'of the impure', and these too are of the kind of the impure: the donkey's urine is forbidden
[version 2] horses' and camels' urine raised no question because people do not drink it; the question was the donkey's, which people drink and which is good for jaundice
Rav Sheshet [version 2]: you learned it -- that which comes out of the impure is impure, and these too come from the impure
the baraita: why did they say bees' honey is permitted? because they gather it into their bodies and do not draw it from their bodies
the stam: he [Rav Sheshet] spoke according to R' Ya'akov
R' Ya'akov: honey -- the Merciful One permitted it
R' Ya'akov: 'yet this you may eat of all flying swarming things' (Lev 11:21) -- this you eat, and you do not eat an impure flying swarming thing
rather: the impure flying thing you do not eat, but you do eat what an impure flying thing swarms out -- and what is that? bees' honey
might one [include] even the honey of gazin and wasps? you said: no
[and what did you see?] I include bees' honey, which has no qualifying name, and exclude the honey of gazin and wasps, which has a qualifying name
the baraita: the honey of gazin and wasps is pure and permitted to eat
the stam: whose view is that baraita? not R' Ya'akov's
the stam: 'pure' -- so [gazin- and wasp-honey] requires intent [to become susceptible to impurity as food]
the baraita: honey in its hive becomes impure with food-impurity without intent
the discharges of a fallow deer: the Rabbis thought to say they are eggs and forbidden
Rav Safra: it is the seed of a hart, which goes after the hind; since her womb is narrow she does not couple, so it goes after the fallow deer, and [the seed] falls out
Rav Huna: the skin that comes over the face of a donkey [at birth] is permitted
what is the reason? it is a mere secretion
the baraita: the skin that comes over the face of a human, whether alive or dead, is pure -- is it not [that] both he and his mother are alive, or both he and his mother are dead?
